s1-pin-sources.summaryMarkdown: PIN-1 met. `PinSource` has only `Project`/`Default` (`project`/`default`); `GpuxProfile`, `GPUX_CHECKOUT`, `Project::is_gpux_checkout` and the `gpux-checkout` fixture are gone, and no reference remains in `src/` or `tests/` outside the neutral `gpux-testkit` member names used as negative cases. `Pins::resolve` applies one rule (project key, else `DEFAULTS`; build tools `None` without a key; system image follows the platform pin and its source); module docs list two sources and the `DEFAULTS` comment names no library. The new `tests/pin_sources.rs` group covers a `gpux-testkit` workspace getting all defaults, declared Android pins as `project` regardless of member names (cargo and files-only discovery), the exhaustive two-variant source, and doctor text/JSON showing only `project`/`default`. Rewritten `project_pins`, `doctor` and `setup_android` tests encode the generic rule. Stale project-domain memory (rules naming the gpux-checkout profile) is for post-epic memory sync per the declared supersession; README is DOC-2 (sprint 4).

s2-entry-crates.summaryMarkdown: All eight criteria are met. `entry_dependencies` resolves keys against normal declarations only (rename, target table, features, default-features, optional, path/git/registry) with both errors; features are forwarded generically with no invented `devkit`; every entry crate is seeded from the workspace lock only when the project has one (checked before the graph's `cargo metadata` can write it), and the web block keeps only wasm-bindgen/futures; patches are selected by the single feature-aware `AppGraph` and rendered as TOML into all three entry crates; `--android-devkit` checks the `devkit` feature before the toolchain and the bridge message names no tool. Each task has its own new test group; finding s2-lock-no-workspace-lock-with-patch is resolved and covered by `tests/app_entry_lockfile.rs`.

s3-assets-android.summaryMarkdown: All five criteria are met. Fonts stage once through the ordinary package-asset path with the name lookup, extra root and `resolved_package_dir` deleted; the app's `platform/web/index.html` or the neutral fallback is rendered before `cargo build` with exactly the three placeholders (adjacent ones included) and unknown tokens refused with token, path and line; `android_java_dirs` come from the graph the build compiles (including the `devkit` feature under `--android-devkit`), validated, sorted, deduplicated and passed as `-PrayxAndroidJavaDirs` only when declared. Each task has its own new test group. Findings S3-JAVA-DEVKIT-FEATURES and S3-WEB-ADJACENT-PLACEHOLDERS are resolved with regression tests.

s4-guard-docs.summaryMarkdown: All five criteria hold. The guard (tests/library_agnostic.rs) tokenizes on [A-Za-z0-9_-], normalizes case and -/_, applies the exact/prefix package deny list plus the source-only page-glue rules, strips every `#[cfg(test)] mod name { }` block with a brace matcher that skips strings, raw strings, char literals and comments while keeping line numbers, skips `#[cfg(test)] mod x;` files (asserts src/app/test_support.rs), and fails on stale allowlist entries. The allowlist is minimal: four entries with reasons (gpux prose in cli.rs, setup/mod.rs, setup/linux.rs; the `rayx-devkit-android` registry dir, documented as CLI vocabulary); `--branches` in guest.rs needs no entry because it tokenizes as `--branches`. GUARD-2 covers normal/dev/build/target/workspace dependency tables (keys and `package` renames) and Cargo.lock names. docs/app-project.md documents every DOC-1 item with neutral names (fallback page checked byte-for-byte against FALLBACK_WEB_PAGE), README pins and pointer match DOC-2, CLAUDE.md == AGENTS.md. release-plz.toml keeps both settings and renders Migration footers as an indented line under the commit (whitespace control verified); docs/releasing.md states the full 1.x policy. Non-blocking notes: the release-plz.toml comment above release_commits also changed (it carried the removed feat! advice, so rewording it is in the spirit of POL-1); in rendered Markdown the two-space indented Migration line is a lazy continuation of the bullet, which the criterion's own example accepts.

s5-release-1-4.summaryMarkdown: Checked the 1.4.0 release against primary sources. `v1.3.0..origin/main` has no breaking markers (count `0`). PR #9 is merged as `6528eb1`, changes only `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` and `CHANGELOG.md`, and every check passed on its final head. The tag `v1.4.0` points to `6528eb1`. Release run 39172926483 succeeded, and the release is published (not a draft or prerelease) with six archives, their `.sha256` files, `sha256.sum` and both installers. The CHANGELOG 1.4.0 section has six `Migration:` notes and no `[**breaking**]` marker, which matches the POL-2 preview excerpt. Only the changelog body and a comment changed in `release-plz.toml`, and the release workflows and `dist-workspace.toml` are untouched. On this Mac `rayx --version` prints `rayx 1.4.0`, and `rayx doctor --json` in a bare workspace reports only the `default` pin source. Finding `s5-rel1-commit-count` is resolved by `f24b56c`, which changes only that line to "The 18 commits", and the breaking-marker count on `v1.3.0..origin/main` still prints `0`.

s6-devkit-graph.summaryMarkdown: `build_android_app_with_toolchain` now derives `built_feature_selection(features, options)` once and shadows `features`, so the Java dirs, the Android entry manifest (and its graph-selected `[patch]` entries) and package-asset staging share the selection the native build compiles; cargo-ndk's `--features devkit` is unchanged and `validate_for` holds because `ensure_devkit_contract` runs first. `app::android::devkit_graph_tests` proves on a fixture app with `devkit = ["dep:store_backend", "dep:devkit_assets"]` (auto mode) that the patch and the devkit-only asset package appear only in the devkit build; its third test pins the single-selection wiring by source text. check-devkit-graph, check-java-dirs-gradle, check-android-devkit, fmt and clippy pass at revision 54.

final.summaryMarkdown:
**Passed.** The integrated `v1.3.0..HEAD` implementation plus the corrective sprint s6-devkit-graph meets all 23 criteria.

F-FINAL-DEVKIT-GRAPH is resolved: `build_android_app_with_toolchain` derives `built_feature_selection(features, options)` once, so an `--android-devkit` build's Java dirs, entry manifest (graph-selected `[patch]` entries) and package-asset staging share the selection the native build compiles; `app::android::devkit_graph_tests` covers the patch and a devkit-only asset package. cargo-ndk arguments are unchanged.

Everything else holds as reviewed before: one graph walker (`app::graph`) for assets, patches and Java dirs; generic `entry_dependencies` and feature forwarding; lockfile seeding of every entry crate; TOML-serialized patches; the app-owned web page with fail-fast placeholder checks and the neutral fallback; pins from project or default only; the library guard over `src/`, `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` with a minimal, self-checking allowlist; docs, README, CLAUDE.md = AGENTS.md and the 1.x release policy match the code; v1.4.0 is released (PR #9 touching only `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock`/`CHANGELOG.md`, six archives, checksums, both installers, `rayx 1.4.0` installed here, no breaking markers). The entry-crate `default` (`<lib>/f`) limitation is deferred by the coordinator to an owner follow-up, as ENTRY-2 keeps today's meaning.

findings.descriptionMarkdown: Resolved: `write_generated_rust_manifest` records whether the workspace has a `Cargo.lock` before the graph's `cargo metadata` can write one and seeds the entry lock only when it did; the no-lock test now keeps the `[patch]` table and proves no entry lock is written for all three targets.

**Expected:** `android_java_dirs` are collected from the app's graph for the features the Android build actually enables (JAVA-1: 'for the selected features'; d-android-java-dirs: only the graph for the selected features contributes, and it is the graph cargo builds).

**Observed:** `build_android_app_with_toolchain` (src/app/android.rs) calls `app.android_java_dirs(features)` with the user's selection, but with `--android-devkit` the cargo-ndk build adds `--features devkit` (same function, `if options.devkit`). An app's `devkit` feature typically enables a dependency (RayX apps: `devkit = ["dep:rayx_devkit"]`), so a package reached only through `devkit` is compiled into the native library while its declared Java directories are not passed to Gradle: the JNI classes it needs are missing from the APK. Conversely the graph used for Java dirs differs from the graph that was built.

**Repair:** compute the Java dirs from the selection the build uses: when `options.devkit`, pass a clone of `features` with `devkit` added (one helper used by both the cargo-ndk feature flag and `android_java_dirs`). Add a case to `tests/app_android_java_dirs.rs` or `java_dirs_gradle_tests`: a fixture package behind the app's `devkit` feature that declares a Java dir is included in the Gradle property for a devkit build and absent otherwise.

**Expected:** each of the three placeholders is replaced wherever it occurs (WEB-1), only an unknown `__RAYX_<NAME>__` token is refused.

**Observed:** `substitute_page` (src/app/wasm.rs) takes the token to end at the *last* `__` of the `[A-Z0-9_]` run, so two placeholders written back to back (`__RAYX_TITLE____RAYX_DIAGNOSTICS__`) or a placeholder followed by an uppercase/underscore run containing `__` (`__RAYX_TITLE__ABC__`) is refused as one unknown token instead of being replaced.

**Repair:** at each `__RAYX_` first try the known placeholders as prefixes (`rest[start..].starts_with(name)`); only when none matches, report the shortest `__RAYX_<NAME>__` token (first `__` after at least one name character). Add a unit case for adjacent placeholders.

The REL-1 record in `docs/manual-verification.md` says "The 19 commits `v1.3.0..cefab09`". Expected: the record states the real count. Observed: `git rev-list --count v1.3.0..cefab09` prints `18`. The range is right and nothing else in the record is wrong. Repair: change `19` to `18` in a `docs(verify)` commit (or drop the number and keep the range).

**An `--android-devkit` build uses two different app graphs.** `src/app/android.rs` `build_android_app_with_toolchain` collects `android_java_dirs` with `built_feature_selection(features, options)` (the selection plus `devkit`, the features the native build compiles through `cargo ndk ... --features devkit`). But in the same build `app.android_rust_manifest(features)` selects the root `[patch]` entries (`generated_patch_tables` -> `AppGraph::resolve`), and `stage_android_package_content(app, features, ...)` discovers package assets, both with the plain `features`, without `devkit`.

*Expected* (d-app-graph: one walker, so "in the app's graph" means the same thing everywhere; PATCH-1/FONT-1: the graph for the selected features; d-entry-patches: the same selection for the same feature selection): a devkit build repeats the `[patch]` entries and stages the package assets of the packages its `devkit` feature reaches, exactly as it already passes their Java directories.

*Observed*: for an app with `devkit = ["dep:x"]` where `x` reaches a root-patched crate or declares a package asset, `rayx app <dir> build|run|deploy|pack android --android-devkit` passes `x`'s Java directories to Gradle but writes an Android entry manifest without `x`'s patch (Cargo then resolves the unpatched crate, dropping the patched lock entry, needing the network and possibly a different version) and stages an APK without `x`'s assets. No test covers patches or package assets for a devkit build; only `a_devkit_build_collects_the_directories_its_devkit_feature_reaches` covers Java dirs.

*Repair*: in `build_android_app_with_toolchain` compute `let built = built_feature_selection(features, options);` once and use it for `android_java_dirs`, `app.android_rust_manifest(&built)` (the cargo-ndk arguments stay unchanged: the native build still adds `--features devkit`, and `<lib>/devkit` in `default` is what that feature enables anyway) and `stage_android_package_content(app, &built, ...)`. Add a test to `app::android::devkit_contract_tests` (or a new named suite) showing that with `devkit = ["dep:store_backend"]` in the fixture app the devkit Android manifest carries the `store_backend` patch and the plain one does not, and that a devkit-only asset package is staged only for the devkit build.
